findings.finding: Frontend and backend disagree on the entire mutating API contract for Roommate Profiles, so create/edit/deactivate/reactivate/message all fail in the integrated build — including the two flows Trust & Safety and Legal specifically required for this MVP (soft-deactivation as the privacy control, and messaging-only contact).
findings.evidence: Create: frontend RoommateProfileFormModal sends seekingType values 'LOOKING_FOR_ROOM'/'HAS_ROOM' (rentals/frontend/src/components/roommates/RoommateProfileFormModal.tsx:25) but the backend Prisma enum RoommateSeekingType is HAS_ROOM/NEEDS_ROOM (schema.prisma:274-277), and the form also sends keys `moveIn`/`audiencePreference` while the backend's .strict() profileCreateSchema requires `moveInTimeframe`/`audiencePref` (roommateProfiles.ts:46-58) — .strict() rejects unknown keys, so every create attempt 400s. Edit: frontend calls `api.patch('/roommate-profiles/{id}', data)` (lib/api.ts:226) but the backend only exposes `PATCH /roommate-profiles/me` scoped to req.user.id, with no `/:id` PATCH route (roommateProfiles.ts:176-192) → 404. Deactivate: frontend calls `api.delete('/roommate-profiles/{id}')` (lib/api.ts:227) but the backend has no DELETE route at all, only `POST /roommate-profiles/me/deactivate` (roommateProfiles.ts:194-207) → 404. Reactivate: frontend calls `PATCH /roommate-profiles/{id}/reactivate` (lib/api.ts:228) but the backend implements `POST /roommate-profiles/me/reactivate` (roommateProfiles.ts:209-222) → 404. Messaging: frontend posts to the generic `POST /messages/conversations` with `{roommateProfileId, body}` (lib/api.ts:202-203), but that route's .strict() schema requires `listingId` and rejects unknown keys (messages.ts:21-24,98-101) → validation failure; the backend's actual `POST /roommate-profiles/:id/message` endpoint (roommateProfiles.ts:261-321) is never invoked by the frontend.
findings.recommendedAction: Reconcile the contract before this can be considered a working, reviewable feature: align enum values (HAS_ROOM/NEEDS_ROOM), field names (moveInTimeframe/audiencePref), and route/verb/path for edit (PATCH /roommate-profiles/me), deactivate (POST /roommate-profiles/me/deactivate), reactivate (POST /roommate-profiles/me/reactivate), and messaging (POST /roommate-profiles/:id/message) between rentals/frontend/src/lib/api.ts, the form's Zod schema/types, and the backend router. Re-run this review once the contract is fixed and a manual end-to-end pass (create → browse → message → deactivate → reactivate → report) has actually been exercised, since neither implementer could run the app in their sandbox.

findings.finding: browseQuerySchema on GET /roommate-profiles is a plain z.object (not .strict()), so a client sending the wrong filter key (e.g. frontend's `audiencePreference` vs backend's expected `audiencePref`) silently no-ops instead of erroring, masking the contract mismatch above rather than surfacing it.
findings.evidence: roommateProfiles.ts:82-90 (browseQuerySchema has no .strict()) vs frontend sending `audiencePreference` as a query key in app/roommates/page.tsx:48.
findings.recommendedAction: Low priority relative to the mutating-route mismatches above; consider .strict() (or an explicit allow-list) on the browse query schema once the contract is aligned, purely to fail loudly on future drift.

findings.finding: The existing-conversation lookup for roommate messaging uses `participants: { every: { userId: { in: [callerId, ownerId] } } }`, which is only a correct 2-party match because conversations created by this route always have exactly those two participants; the query itself doesn't assert both specific users are present (an `every` over an empty/partial relation would vacuously match).
findings.recommendedAction: Not currently exploitable given how conversations are created, but consider an explicit `AND: [{participants: {some: {userId: callerId}}}, {participants: {some: {userId: ownerId}}}]` for correctness/defense-in-depth once other fixes land.

findings.finding: Object-level authorization, field-level privacy (no email/phone/precise location anywhere in RoommateProfile schema or PUBLIC_SELECT), IDOR protection (all mutations scoped to req.user.id, never a client-supplied :id), and reuse of the existing Report model/pattern are all implemented correctly and match the designer/T&S/Legal guidance.
findings.recommendedAction: No action needed — noted so this isn't lost among the contract-mismatch findings.

notes: Reviewed the actual integrated diff (schema.prisma, roommateProfiles.ts, messages.ts, admin.ts, socketServer.ts, and the frontend roommates page/components/api.ts/types) directly rather than relying on the implementer/integrator summaries. Access-control, IDOR, and privacy-field-exposure design is sound and matches the prerequisite specs, but the backend and frontend were built against different, unreconciled API contracts (enum values, field names, HTTP verbs, and route paths all diverge across create/edit/deactivate/reactivate/message), so the merged feature does not actually work end-to-end. The integrator's report states the two branches merged with no file overlap and therefore needed no reconciliation, but did not verify cross-branch contract compatibility — that gap is the root cause here. This must be fixed and re-verified before this can be called a production-ready MVP.
